detail.abstract: We study the revenue-maximizing product-selection and ranking problem under the MNL-Rank consider-then-choose model introduced by Derakhshan et al. (2022). This model captures common search dynamics in e-commerce environments, where customers sequentially inspect products in the order selected by the platform and subsequently make an MNL-based purchase decision from the products they have considered. Specifically, the platform selects both the products to display and their relative ranking, while customers inspect the displayed products sequentially in rank order, subject to position-dependent search costs. Because the attractiveness of the products encountered affects how far customers search, the platform's product-selection and ranking decisions interact endogenously with customers' consideration sets. We develop a polynomial-time approximation scheme for the resulting revenue-maximization problem. This result establishes that near-optimal joint product-selection and ranking decisions remain computationally tractable under a wellestablished consider-then-choose model of customer search. Our algorithmic approach combines efficient enumeration, approximate dynamic programming, linearization, and pruning arguments. We also study the data-driven estimation of the MNL-Rank model. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first procedure for estimating this model from observed search, click, and purchase data. Using Expedia search and booking data, we compare MNL-Rank against an otherwise comparable benchmark in which the consideration-set formation process is exogenous to the identities and attractiveness of the products in the displayed ranking. Our results reveal that the MNL-Rank model achieves a higher out-of-sample purchase-event log-likelihood on each of the three Expedia sites considered, increasing log-likelihood by 2.2-4.2% across sites. These findings provide empirical evidence that allowing customers' search paths to respond endogenously to the attractiveness of the products encountered can meaningfully improve choice prediction.

detail.abstract: Psychologists increasingly use large language models (LLMs) as experimental participants, but an effect in such a silicon sample supports a process theory only if the LLM's response arises causally through representing the intermediate psychological states, or constructs, before it is produced. detail.abstract: Problem definition: We study the order fulfillment problem for an on-demand delivery platform with full-time and crowdsourced couriers receiving heterogeneous (high-price and low-price) orders. Upon an order arrival, the platform decides whether to serve the order and, if so, which courier type to assign it to. Methodology/results: We formulate an infinite-horizon discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) to maximize the platform's expected total discounted profit. Under value-function conditions, we characterize an optimal policy with thresholds based on the numbers of available couriers. The optimal policy maximizes the profit using two mechanisms. First, courier holding (CH) proactively rejects a low-price order to hold a courier for a high-price order. Second, assignment optimization (AO) chooses a courier by balancing the wage difference with the opportunity profit difference. Numerical studies using real-world data suggest expected discounted profit improvements of up to 33.74% over an industrial benchmark in instances with both order types and both courier types. Adding CH first contributes 24.36%, followed by 9.38% from AO through courier priority correction. We further extend the MDP to incorporate high-price order cancellations and characterize the corresponding optimal policy. Managerial implications: The platform should serve high-price orders whenever a courier is available but may reject low-price orders to reserve capacity for more profitable orders. CH yields substantial benefit if crowdsourced couriers are the majority, orders are balanced in composition, or the order price gap is large. AO yields substantial benefit relative to the industrial priority rule if low-price orders are the majority, couriers are balanced in composition, or full-time couriers have a significantly lower wage than crowdsourced couriers. CH with an appropriate fixed courier priority matches or closely approximates the optimal profit.

detail.abstract:
This study shows that better matching can reduce monopsony power and provides empirical evidence using U.S. data from 2019 to 2025. If better matching weakens monopsony power, its effects operate through both higher productivity and reduced labor market power, with the latter generating efficiency gains. This study captures better matches as worker-specific job openings, identified by matching workers’ current job titles with the titles of posted vacancies. The idea is that openings related to a worker’s current job title are more likely to provide a better match than unrelated openings. This measure captures actual job opportunities available in the local labor market at a given point in time, whereas prior studies have measured potential job opportunities.

This study examines whether greater worker-specific job openings increase the probability of separation from the current firm to assess whether better matching increases labor supply elasticity, and whether firms respond by strengthening promotion incentives. This study also considers initial job opportunities when workers join their current firms and the effects of their colleagues’ job opportunities in these estimations. Linking online job posting data with online worker-level data, the analysis employs an instrumental variable.

As a result, worker-specific job openings increase the probability of separation, with the largest effects occurring a few months before separation and smaller effects further from separation. Better initial job opportunities reduce the effect of current worker-specific job openings on separation. Interestingly, a higher share of colleagues experiencing an increase in job openings reduces separation. Regarding firms’ responses, an increase in worker-specific job openings increases promotion and decreases the probability of staying without promotion. Analysis by colleagues’ job level shows that an increase in worker-specific job openings among higher-level colleagues increases promotion in the software and finance job categories, but not in the teacher and nurse job categories.

Therefore, the finding that better matching increases separation suggests a reduction in monopsony power. This effect reflects not just workers’ own opportunities but also those of their colleagues. Firms also respond to changing outside options. However, this response is not observed in some labor markets where prior studies prior studies suggest an important role for monopsony power. Linking matching and monopsony provides a better understanding of the potential for simultaneous improvements in productivity and reductions in labor market distortions.

detail.abstract: Contemporary sustainability research remains heavily constrained by a reliance on technological interventions to mitigate ecological decay. This commentary critiques this paradigm by demonstrating how technical efficiency often acts as an accelerator of resource extraction rather than a solution to material dependency. By integrating behavioral metrics into traditional ecological-impact models, this article shifts the analytical lens from external engineering fixes to internal structural transformation. We utilize a radical political economy framework to trace how the structural legacy of neoliberal Structural Adjustment Programmes (SAPs) has marketised public architecture, engineering a matrix of elite capture and acute institutional insolvency. This systemic crisis is exposed through the 2026 Kenyan public university financial collapse and the historic 28-day countrywide solidarity strike executed across all cadres by UASU, KUSU, and KUDHEIHA. Crucially, we demonstrate that this mobilization was not a narrow dispute over academic salaries, but an organic, multi-cadre class rejection of the peripheral capitalist state, uniting academic faculty with agricultural, support, and non-teaching workers. We model collective psychological wellbeing as a non-linear inverse function of the wealth distribution gap (the Gini index). This demonstrates that systemic inequality drives destabilising, high-emission conspicuous consumption as a defense mechanism against relative deprivation. Finally, drawing on the re-formulated Coupled Climate-Economy-Biosphere (CoCEB) framework, we propose that Universal Basic Income (UBI) serves as a critical macroeconomic vehicle for Samir Amin's doctrine of "delinking." By funding UBI through a designated fraction of the global warming abatement share, the state contractually decompresses inequality, bypasses centralized nodes prone to elite capture, and prevents post-colonial resources from being siphoned into top-heavy carbon monopolies managed by Western metropolitan NGOs, providing a formula-driven path toward securing our shared progress.

detail.abstract: Falling technology costs are making solar PV the dominant source of renewable capacity growth and central to achieving net-zero emissions. Yet utility-scale solar's substantial land requirements place it in direct competition with agriculture. Exploiting China's unprecedented prioritization of food security after 2012 as an exogenous shock, we find that high-yield counties experienced an 11.2-percentage-point decline in new-deployment probability, nearly half the sample mean, and a 0.122 km 2 decline in annual PV area, equal to average annual county deployment, relative to low-yield counties. Moreover, the policy appears to overshoot: its effects extend to non-cropland and nearby low-yield counties and are no stronger in counties highly productive in China's most import-dependent staple crop. Mechanism evidence points to top-down enforcement rather than voluntary local adjustment, with restrictions on county governments' land conveyance to PV developers as the potential channel. Under highly conservative assumptions, we estimate forgone annual CO 2 abatement of 9.2-14.3 million tons, while finding no measurable increases in grain output or cultivated-land area. These findings from the world's largest solar market highlight the food-energy conflict as a substantial barrier to the global energy transition.

detail.abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) procedures generate structured, legally dense documentary corpora well suited to large language model (LLM) processing, yet the institutional conditions under which generative AI can be safely and sustainably integrated into SEA workflows remain underexplored, particularly from the perspective of the competent authority. detail.abstract: Project 2029 is the banner under which opponents of the Trump Administration have debated a counter platform to the radical destruction of Trump's chaotic second-term program. This debate has thus far failed to adopt a transitional justice (TJ) approach, even though the TJ literature directly addresses how societies come to terms with and transition away from the trauma of large-scale abuses and repressive regimes. Instead, the leading proposals for Project 2029, such as those centered around combatting the "Annoyance Economy," are distinctly modest, in stark contrast to the approaches of other societies in similar situations throughout history and around the globe. From the denazification of Europe, the decommunization of the former Soviet bloc, and the transformation of South Africa to a new democracy post-apartheid, a remarkably consistent set of TJ tools and mechanisms have emerged to help societies re-set the legal and political order after major ruptures. This article helps fill in what an analogous project might look like in the post-Trump United States with an emphasis not just on backward-looking accountability, but on the vision of a human-centered future toward which we could build. The piece starts with the leading comprehensive account of TJ, developed by Colleen Murphy, and the tools and mechanisms entailed. The article then shows the history of those tools in the U.S. and how they have been tacitly wielded by Trump proponents in Project 2025. Finally, the piece illustrates how we might apply that frame and its tools to generate specific and plausible proposals for Project 2029 in a signature domain, health policy.

detail.abstract: Obsolescence is a central variable for understanding innovation. detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the predictive power of monthly implied-volatility (IV) spreads on underlying stock returns differs across firms with different valuation-related characteristics. Hard-to-value firms offer greater scope for investor disagreement and temporary price pressure, so option-implied signals may carry more incremental information about their subsequent returns. Using U.S. optionable stocks from July 2001 through August 2023, we construct a hard-to-value (HTV) index from market-to-book, R&D intensity, and idiosyncratic volatility. In firm-and-month fixed-effects regressions using OptionMetrics Version 6 implied volatilities, the IV-spread interaction with HTV is positive and statistically significant, with the largest estimated slope among firms classified as hard to value on all three dimensions. The baseline high-minus-low-HTV difference in IV-spread portfolio return spreads is 0.609 percent per month and remains significant after Fama-French five-factor adjustment. The interaction also remains positive and significant after controls for IV skew, observable short-sale demand, vendor-implied borrowing rates, and VIX exposure. On a common sample, the Version 6 and Version 7 Base implied-volatility constructions produce similar HTV portfolio differentials of 0.618 and 0.607 percent per month, respectively, while their regression interactions are significant in different specifications, with firm fixed effects for Version 6 and in pooled and Fama-MacBeth regressions for Version 7 Base. detail.abstract: Falling technology costs are making solar PV the dominant source of renewable capacity growth and central to achieving net-zero emissions. Yet utility-scale solar's substantial land requirements place it in direct competition with agriculture. Under highly conservative assumptions, we estimate forgone annual CO 2 abatement of 9.2-14.3 million tons, while finding no measurable increases in grain output or cultivated-land area. These findings from the world's largest solar market highlight the food-energy conflict as a substantial barrier to the global energy transition.

detail.abstract: A growing literature shows that democratic institutions, particularly elections, are associated with higher deforestation. To enhance our understanding of the mechanisms driving this relationship, we study the link between the electoral backlash to environmental protection, the incumbents' electoral needs and the behavior of environmental bureaucracies. We argue and show that bureaucratic enforcement follows a politico-economic logic. In response to backlash by voters and producers, politicians strategically alter the implementation of environmental policy, selectively withholding enforcement where expected political costs are highest. Political costs are higher in districts with both electoral value and high extractive potential after deforestation. This creates systematic gaps in enforcement, weakening deterrence and increasing future deforestation. We test this argument in the Brazilian Amazon, tracing step by step the process from backlash to strategic enforcement and, ultimately, environmental outcomes. Strategic enforcement emerges as an important driver of further deforestation. Our findings offer a nuanced understanding of how politics shape environmental outcomes and suggest ways to design more resilient environmental policies.

detail.abstract:
Where Trade Is Felt examines how Canadian municipalities are experiencing and responding to U.S. trade disruption, and what their experiences suggest for Canada’s broader economic response. Developed by the Lawrence National Centre for Policy and Management at Ivey Business School, in collaboration with the Federation of Canadian Municipalities and the City of London, the report draws on responses from 31 municipalities across nine provinces and reflects local conditions reported in May 2026.

The findings show that trade-related pressures are being felt unevenly across communities, with cost pressures, supply-chain disruptions, and investment delays among the most commonly reported impacts. The report also highlights how local economic and industrial profiles shape these experiences, and how municipalities are responding through business outreach, procurement, investment attraction, diversification, and other local measures.

The report argues that municipal intelligence can complement existing economic information and strengthen Canada’s broader Team Canada response. It concludes with options for consideration organized around three pillars—Connect, Coordinate, and Unblock—focused on more consistent municipal intelligence-sharing, improved information flows during periods of disruption, and reducing barriers to a coordinated domestic response.

detail.abstract: Staggered-adoption difference-indifferences (DiD) designs are a workhorse of empirical research in business-school journals. The two-way fixed effects (TWFE) estimator that typically implements them can place negative weights on heterogeneous treatment effects. We ask whether negative weights change published findings by reanalyzing staggered-adoption specifications in business-school journals with journal-wide public replication archives. Following Hull (2026), we use large language model agents to identify eligible specifications, replicate the published TWFE estimate, and re-estimate each specification with the DiD-averaging estimator of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) and the imputation estimator of Borusyak et al. (2024). We re-estimate 355 specifications from 40 papers. Across the 283 DiD-averaging and 306 imputation comparisons that pass Hull's leverage screen, from 28 and 29 papers, TWFE and modern estimates have correlations of 0.61 and 0.70, change sign in 25.1 and 18.0 percent of comparisons, and differ significantly with opposite signs in 10.2 and 7.2 percent. Modern standard errors are 1.61 and 1.30 times those of TWFE. Including the comparisons that fail the screen leaves these figures essentially unchanged. Our results suggest that TWFE and heterogeneity-robust estimators disagree in a non-negligible share of the published staggered designs we re-estimate, and more often than in economics.

detail.abstract: The guarantee on a period-certain annuity reaches heirs only if they claim it. To the heirs the payment is a lottery that does not depend on stock returns, so uncertain settlement is a background risk carried by the bequest. We show that it lowers retirees' stock holdings. A two-period example gives the size of the effect to second order and shows that end-of-life spending, which depletes the estate but not the guarantee, enlarges it. In a life-cycle model with annuity choice, annual portfolio choice and out-of-pocket medical spending matched to the Health and Retirement Study, settlement with probability one-half lowers the stock share at 65 of a retiree with a strong bequest motive from 1.00 to 0.78, whereas a certain loss with the same expected value lowers it only to 0.93. The effect requires that the guarantee be bought and that the household hold bonds, which happens at low equity premia or high risk aversion, and it fades as the guarantee runs off. It falls mainly on retirees in poor health. Medical spending makes the guarantee more attractive and keeps it in demand at lower settlement probabilities, while at low risk aversion stocks crowd it out. The welfare cost is at most 0.27% of initial wealth (0.40% for retirees in poor health), because retirees adjust both their annuities and their portfolios. detail.abstract: People have potential in many fields, but most models of how opportunity should be allocated consider one. This article extends an agent-based model of allocating opportunity by potential to many fields. Each person has a potential in every field, works and develops mainly in one, and is observed through noisy tests; each field has its own budget. Six assignment rules are compared: absolute advantage, comparative advantage, market clearing, self-selection, random assignment and centralised admission by deferred acceptance. Over 88,000 simulations of 10,000 agents yield five results. First, the choice between absolute and comparative advantage turns on whether field capacities are fixed: with fixed budgets, absolute advantage crowds the field with the most able population and loses up to 38 per cent of successes, whereas when budgets follow people it is the best rule. Market clearing is within 2.5 per cent of the best rule in every setting. Second, the cost of absolute advantage grows with the number of fields. Third, because learning and development are field-specific, people stay in their first field, and allowing reassignment changes successes by between-8 and +1.5 per cent. Fourth, rules for allocating opportunity within a field carry over from the single-field case. Fifth, centralised admission with full preference lists matches the best rules without anyone knowing comparative advantages, but limiting the number of choices is costly. Who goes where matters as much as who gets what.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how the destination of deposits withdrawn during bank runs shapes systemic liquidity stress. We incorporate deposit reallocation into a run-driven network contagion model and show that it weakly mitigates stress, acting through two channels. On the demand side, reallocation reduces the propagation of interbank callbacks, and on the supply side it increases the payments that shocked banks can make to their depositors. The relief depends on where deposits are redirected, as well as on how much is redirected. Demand-side relief is larger when deposits reach banks that are more central in the propagation of callbacks, whereas supply-side relief requires that deposits reach banks whose repayments channel liquidity back to the shocked banks. We calibrate the model to the 25 largest US Bank Holding Companies at 2006q4 and 2022q4, two systems that differ in the size of liquidity buffers relative to interbank exposures, and evaluate a gravity rule motivated by evidence on deposit flows. When the channels are active, the rule captures a large share of the available demand-side relief in 2006 but only a small part of it in 2022, and delivers little or none of the supply-side relief at both dates. Stress tests that abstract from deposit reallocation may overstate liquidity stress, to an extent that depends on the structure of the system.

detail.abstract: Capitalism involves a tradeoff between economic efficiency and wealth inequality. The land market has some distinctive characteristics that may make the tradeoff particularly unfavorable. Inelastic supply of land may allow landowners to accumulate wealth rapidly. Land is both an input and an investment on its own. Since capital gains are uncertain, the cost of using land is uncertain. The resulting variation in the expected cost of using land can lower economic efficiency by distorting investment decisions. Agglomeration economies make the notion of market fundamentals elusive and may reward herding. Herding can lead to overdevelopment in some communities and underdevelopment in some other communities. The land tax proposed by George (1879) could address these issues, but it could also undermine the land right and increase the cost of using land. This paper proposes an alternative scheme that equalizes capital gains at a modest level through taxes and tax credits. detail.abstract: The series studies structures-firms, markets, codes, mechanical systems, societiesthrough two questions: what does a structure refuse to do, and what enforces the refusal? One of its central ideas is that a stable structure rests on a short list of prohibitions, kept by guards inside it, within which a great deal is left free. The list is its non-convention; a guard is a quantity the structure keeps, and cannot change without breaking a prohibition. This first article states the idea and tests it on four structures in which every term has a name: a body around a centre of attraction, prices with no arbitrage, heat and work, and voting rules, where the list must be shortened before it can be met. The tests show that prohibitions with guards select a law, that the guards can be counted and watched, and that five further things-a convention, a reach, a strength, a home for the guard and a count-are used in every test. The tools the tests call for are named in the closing section. What the idea leads to is a way of reading a structure before it changes: the guards that came from one law rather than from the setting are the ones to watch, their drift is readable before the law is known to have changed, and the number of guards says how many ways a difficulty can build while every indicator holds.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a quantitative study of the prospects of the Greek macroeconomy in the medium and long term. The vehicle of analysis is a medium-scale dynamic general equilibrium model calibrated to Greek data. The model includes the main sectors: households, private firms, private banks, the National Central Bank in the Eurosystem and the public sector. We work in three steps. First, we solve the model when policy and other exogenous variables are set as in the most recent data. This solution serves as a departure point for the simulations that follow next. In the second step, we study the transition path of this economy when dynamics are driven by the repayment of the official loans taken from EU institutions since Greece's sovereign debt crisis in the previous decade. Our simulations show that this repayment, other things equal, will have long-lasting recessionary implications and will require systematic primary fiscal surpluses. Third, we search for structural and policy reforms that can mitigate, and hopefully more than offset, these recessionary effects. Following the literature on policy reforms, we change structural parameters and policy variables so as to reduce the gap between Greece and best practice in the EU in key areas. We close with policy takeaways.
